'Precocious little shit,' she snaps. Bill raises his voice, 'I'm not defending her. I'm not blaming her, because I'm on your side. How can we fight when I'm on your side? I don't expect her to act any differently when her father is a selfish son-of-a-bitch.' Barbara shouts back, 'Be a father! Help me!' Bill responds, 'I am her father, goddamn it!' name: Barbara and Bill Question Violet About Beverly's Disappearance
description: Barbara and Bill sit at the linoleum table on the screened-in back porch as Violet stands nearby, watching Charlie and Mattie Fae drive away in the Cadillac. Barbara presses Violet for details about when Beverly left. Violet recalls it was Saturday morning, after they ate biscuits and gravy made by the Indian girl. She says Beverly simply walked out the door, got in his truck, and never returned. Barbara expresses disbelief, asking why he would leave without a word. Violet explains she didn’t think much of it at first, assuming he’d gone on a drinking binge, but by Sunday she began to worry. She mentions the safety deposit box, saying she and Beverly had an agreement that if anything happened to one of them, the other would empty the box before the bank could seal it. Barbara scoffs, calling her a cynic. Bill interjects, confirming that estates typically freeze such accounts during probate. Violet says she waited for the bank to open on Monday, emptied the box, then reported Beverly missing. Barbara is upset that Ivy only called her that day. Violet claims she didn’t want to worry her. Bill asks if there was a fight or some incident that led to Beverly’s departure. Violet says no, though they’d had their share, but insists he just left. Barbara mutters that maybe he needed time away from Violet. Violet responds with quiet bitterness, then reflects on how she once found Beverly’s silence and mystery alluring, how he always seemed to know something no one else did, and how that used to feel like power.

name: Violet Remembers Beverly's Quiet Charm
description: Violet sits at the linoleum table, watching her daughter Barbara react to the news of Beverly's disappearance. In response to Barbara's sharp words, Violet begins to speak about the early days of her marriage. She recalls how she was drawn to Beverly's silence, how he would stand in a room knowing everything, saying nothing, just smiling slightly. She remembers thinking it was the sexiest thing in the world—that quiet confidence, that unspoken intelligence. Her voice softens as she describes falling in love with his mystery, a feeling that lingers even now, years later, in the empty space he left behind.

name: Violet Watches Charlie and Mattie Fae Drive Away
